newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong quake in southern Japan injures six.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake in southern Japan injures six.

text.p: A moderately strong earthquake measuring 6.2 on the Richter scale shook the southern Japanese island of Kyushu on Wednesday, causing minor injuries to at least six people, government officials said.
The Japan Meteorological Agency said the earthquake hit the island at 5.31 p.m. (0831 GMT) with the epicentre near the city of Kagoshima, 800 km (500 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
A number of fairly strong tremors continued to shake the region after the initial quake, and agency officials warned that aftershocks could continue to hit the area for a while.
At least six people suffered minor injuries from objects falling from shelves, a Kagoshima prefectural government official told Reuters.
"At least one person fractured the right arm, but the rest we hear are minor injuries such as scratches from broken glass or being hit by falling objects," the spokesman said.
"We don't have the final confirmation yet, but the number of injuries may rise to about 15," he said.
At least five houses were damaged, and some concrete fences collapsed due to the quake, Kagoshima prefectural police officials said. Some roads were also blocked due to landslides, they said.
Operations at Sendai nuclear power plant, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Kagoshima, were not disturbed by the tremor, Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc, officials said.
A quake of such magnitude can cause severe damage.
